description:
Make every preview and read run through the same mutation session and captured image as the operation it previews, so that a preview cannot disagree with the result and every mutation derives its coupled state inside its own plan. Today several commands keep parallel preview pipelines, state derivations, lease checks, configuration loaders and storage primitives beside the captured-image path.

## Background

Mutation derivation:

- **Readiness.** The dependent-readiness cascade has three implementations. Deletion derives dependent Ready transitions inside its own plan (`crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:55-144`). Single-issue update and automatic Done run `check_auto_transitions` after the commit (`issue.rs:519-524,795-797,804`); it lists every issue and publishes one further session per dependent. The bulk path runs none.
- **Field derivations.** Assign, unassign, gate add and gate remove each have a dedicated captured mutation (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:1512-1600`) beside the general field update. The two paths write different events for the same change.
- **Lease checks.** There are three lease-check implementations, each formatting the same missing-lease message (`mod.rs:768,3333`; `crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:317`). The legacy `require_active_lease` (`mod.rs:3317`) runs before, and outside, the publishing session at six sites (`issue.rs:678,719`; `crates/jit/src/commands/gate.rs:726,770,816,1033`).

Previews:

- **Bulk preview.** `preview_bulk_update` (`crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs:444-619`) reimplements write validation. For each matched issue it lists every issue and reloads the gate registry, which costs $O(M \cdot N)$. It hand-projects the post-update issue and evaluates only local rules, from the disk cache. Apply enforces graph rules that the preview skips, so the two can disagree.
- **Archive preview.** `plan_archive_target` (`crates/jit/src/commands/archive.rs:178-303`) repeats the execute planner `capture_archive_plan` (`archive.rs:505-828`) step for step, over about 800 lines of storage-only helpers (`crates/jit/src/storage/artifact_planning.rs`, `storage/artifact_discovery.rs`).
  - `archive_candidates` plans each candidate from scratch, re-reading configuration, all issues and the event log each time.
  - Container-destination evidence is acquired by hand twice, and the `.jit-container` marker name is formatted at more than five sites.
  - Embedded-owner discovery walks reachability once per document reference and resolves every reference again on each walk (`crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_discovery.rs:501-553`).

Configuration and declarations:

- **Disk caches.** The executor keeps four disk-backed `OnceLock` caches for rules and configuration (`mod.rs:2038-2058`) beside the image declarations that write paths use.
- **Assembly.** `JitConfig::load` and the image declaration path assemble configuration in two separate pipelines. `ConfigurationDeclarations` mirrors five fields of the config it wraps (`crates/jit/src/declarations/mod.rs:30-42`).
- **Repeated reads.** `get_hierarchy_config` re-reads three TOML files from disk (`crates/jit/src/config_manager.rs:302`) and has 13 call sites. Declarations are parsed more than once within one mutation (`mod.rs:2830,3023`; `issue.rs:65`).
- **Gate presets.** Presets have three readers. `PresetManager` does raw filesystem I/O outside storage on a hardcoded path (`crates/jit/src/gate_presets/manager.rs:17-95`), and the memory backend copies its listing.
- **Gate evidence.** Precheck evidence capture (`mod.rs:622`) is a parallel variant of gate-evaluation capture (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs:321`), and the prompt size limit is enforced twice (`gate_check.rs:385,1278`). `check_gate_with` re-derives the issue, the registry and the gate from the same image several times.

Storage primitives:

- **Image copies.** Each capture round deep-clones the whole captured image (`crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs:606,757`). `MaterializationPlan::new` clones it again (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:720`), and `ensure_session_image` compares it byte for byte (`repository_state_store.rs:844`).
- **Redo apply.** Redo apply walks each parent chain three times, with two `lstat` calls per component, and fsyncs the parent directory after every operation (`crates/jit/src/storage/redo_apply.rs:130-320`).
- **No-follow primitives.** These live in the session module (`repository_state_store.rs:1511-1912`), which forms an import cycle with `redo_apply.rs:17`. The leaf-open sequence is written four times, and record commit uses ambient path I/O (`crates/jit/src/storage/redo_record.rs:208,342`).
- **Atomic writes.** There are five atomic-write implementations. The server PID file is written without fsync (`crates/jit/src/commands/serve.rs:85-90`). The claims index uses the fixed temporary name `claims.index.tmp` (`crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs:884-899`).

Layering:

- **Domain errors.** The domain artifact classifier imports `repository_state::ProducerError` and matches it with a wildcard arm (`crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_classifier.rs:799,853`). Two missing-evidence helpers in that module return different error types, and domain code uses `anyhow`.
- **Snapshot export.** Snapshot export re-serializes issues outside the canonical serializer (`crates/jit/src/commands/snapshot.rs:453`) and copies only `config.toml` and `gates.toml` (`snapshot.rs:462`).
- **Duplicated primitives.**
  - Two PID-liveness primitives apply different non-unix policies (`serve.rs:118`; `crates/jit/src/storage/lock_cleanup.rs:16`).
  - `InvariantRegistry::load` reads files (`crates/jit/src/declarations/invariants.rs:144`), although the declarations module is documented as filesystem-free.
  - There are two safe-relative-path validators (`crates/jit/src/domain/repository_inputs.rs:454` and `RootRelativePath::parse`).
  - `SnapshotScope` duplicates `DocumentScope`.
  - `StatusSummary` stores the Backlog count under `open` (`mod.rs:1718`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One pure readiness derivation computes the dependent Ready and Backlog corrections from a projected issue set, and every mutation plan that changes a state or a dependency includes its corrections in its own redo record.
- [hard] REQ-02: No command publishes a follow-up mutation to correct readiness after its primary mutation commits.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each issue field has exactly one derivation. The dedicated assign, unassign, gate-add and gate-remove commands and the general update produce the same issue state and the same events for the same change.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every issue mutation checks leases inside its publishing session against captured claims evidence, through one check. No pre-session lease check remains, and the foreign-lease refusal is defined once.
- [hard] REQ-05: No bulk-update preview exists apart from the apply derivation; bulk apply processes every matched issue in one session and publishes one redo record.
- [hard] REQ-06: Archive preview and candidate listing run the execute planner in one read-only session, and the plan a preview reports equals the plan execute applies over the same image. The storage-only archive planning helpers are deleted.
- [hard] REQ-07: Container-destination evidence is requested by one function, and the container marker name is declared once.
- [hard] REQ-08: Archive planning resolves each artifact reference once per plan and computes reachability once per distinct document root.
- [hard] REQ-09: One pure function assembles `JitConfig` from source bytes. Filesystem loading and image capture both call it, and `ConfigurationDeclarations` carries no field that duplicates the assembled config.
- [hard] REQ-10: The executor holds no disk-backed configuration, rules or namespace cache. Read paths take declarations from a captured image, hierarchy configuration derives from those declarations without a disk read, and each mutation attempt parses its declarations once per captured image.
- [hard] REQ-11: Storage backends supply custom gate-preset bytes keyed by the gate-presets path, listing and lookup are one pure implementation, and no preset file I/O remains outside the storage layer.
- [hard] REQ-12: Gate evaluation and precheck capture their evidence through one function that enforces the prompt size limit, and each evaluation resolves its issue, registry and gate definition once per captured image.
- [hard] REQ-13: Capture rounds and materialization plans share the captured image, without copying it. A session recognizes its own image by an identity token, without comparing bytes.
- [hard] REQ-14: Redo apply opens each distinct parent directory once per record.
- [hard] REQ-15: Redo apply fsyncs each distinct parent directory once per record only after interruption tests at every operation boundary show that the next session completes the record to the committed state. Without that proof, per-operation directory syncs remain and the module rustdoc states why.
- [hard] REQ-16: The no-follow filesystem primitives live in one storage module that both the session and redo apply depend on, with no import cycle, and the leaf-open sequence exists once. The redo-record module only defines the record format, and record commit goes through capability handles.
- [hard] REQ-17: One atomic file-publication function with an explicit durability argument exists. Lease records, the claims sequence counter, worktree identity and server PID file publish through it, each temporary name is unique per writer, and the PID file is synced.
- [hard] REQ-18: The domain layer imports nothing from `repository_state` and returns typed errors. The artifact classifier reports layout violations through a domain type that it matches exhaustively, and resolves missing evidence through one helper.
- [hard] REQ-19: Snapshot export writes the stored bytes of each issue and every declaration file the repository layout defines, read from one captured image.
- [hard] REQ-20: Each of the following has one form:
  - process liveness, as one guarded primitive with one non-unix policy;
  - declaration modules, which only parse, with file reads in storage;
  - safe relative paths, with one validator;
  - snapshot and link-check scopes, with one scope type;
  - type extraction from labels, with one normalisation;
  - no-follow repository file reads, through the shared read primitive;
  - archive destination resolution, with no legacy short-id destination fallback.
- [hard] REQ-21: Archive preview and candidates, declaration reads, gate-preset reads, `jit validate` without `--fix`, `doc check-links` and profile planning and dry runs capture without the repository lock, and each capture is admitted only when no redo record was present and the event log did not grow across it. After a bounded number of refused attempts the read runs under the repository lock, which completes a leftover redo record. A test on both storage backends shows eight readers admitted while a writer holds the repository lock. A benchmark under `dev/benchmarks/` shows that, during a continuous writer, eight concurrent readers complete at least four times as many reads per second as one reader, and that the writer keeps at least 80% of its no-reader throughput, compared with the pre-change binary.
- [hard] REQ-22: Before-and-after measurements under `dev/benchmarks/`, taken by one harness against the pre-change binary, show each claimed cost reduction: bulk-update time at a fixed match count no longer grows with the product of matches and repository issues; archive candidate listing no longer repeats a session per candidate; a mutation parses its declarations once per captured image; and redo apply opens each distinct parent directory once per record, with its directory-sync count as REQ-15 settles it.
- [hard] REQ-23: Every redo record over a present data root appends at least one event. A mutation that derives no domain event appends one generic event naming the files it published, and a delta that writes repository state over a present data root without an event append is rejected before commit. The publication that creates an absent data root is exempt, because a reader observes the root's appearance.

## Notes

- Serves `@/charter/D-22` (REQ-21, REQ-23), `@/charter/D-20` (previews are read-only sessions over the same computation) and `@/charter/D-18`.
- Restores:
  - `@/inv/derived-state-coherence` and `@/inv/event-log` (REQ-01 to REQ-04);
  - `@/inv/convention-convergence`;
  - `@/inv/architecture-dependency-direction` (REQ-16, REQ-18, REQ-20);
  - `@/inv/atomic-writes` (REQ-14 to REQ-17);
  - `@/inv/pid-safety` (REQ-20).
- REQ-15 is conditional because coalescing directory syncs is safe only if replaying the whole record after a crash restores every operation. That claim must be proven against `@/inv/atomic-writes` before syncs move.
- `snapshot export` keeps its locked session: the user excluded its recovery dispatch from the lock-free read scope.
- Lease-enforcement mode resolution is outside this epic. This epic decides where the check runs, not which mode applies.


- Steward note (just-in-time-d5, 2026-11-09): the owning evidence for REQ-12 ("each evaluation resolves its issue, registry and gate definition once per captured image") is the single test added under `6b22ce6d` REQ-02; `700a96dd`, `a869900b` and `a2153a6f` closed without one.
title: Converge previews and coupled derivations on the mutation session
